His weight unbalanced her, and Orela went sideways and down before she'd fully registered what was happening. Her shoulder hit the wall and then his hands were on her shoulders and he was pulling down — not intentionally, just pure animal logic and a drive to go UP — and for one lurching second, they were both going under. Her shoulder slid across the wall. She got her back against it and held, both hands locked in his collar, teeth gritted, the pull of him dragging at her arms with a steady insistence that threatened to twist her loose from her precarious stability. Dwight reached her first, plastering himself against the wall and grabbing her arm with both hands, anchoring. Jake was a half second behind, getting a hand into the back of Danny's collar alongside hers, and the three of them formed a human chain against the wall — Dwight braced and pulling, Orela holding, Jake hauling — working Danny hand over hand out of the current's reach and back toward solid footing. Danny thrashed against the sucking current, panic-born, nearly tearing free from the grip as the three dragged him back towards the wall away from the jets of chaos with everything they had. They got him against the wall and held him there while he fell apart. Danny collapsed against the wall, nearly sliding right back into the water were it not for the boys at each arm holding him upright, coughing up water in long, wracking heaves, one hand braced against Dwight's shoulder without appearing to register it was there. Blood tracked down from somewhere above his hairline, thinned to pink by the water. His lip was split. The whole of him slumped like dead weight, eyes barely tracking. Orela’s hands went straight to the soaked folds of his robe. The fabric clung to his frame, leather straps pinning it against him, water pouring off it in sheets. "Off," she snapped, already tugging at the collar. "You may as well have worn a damned anchor. What kind of idiot wears twenty layers in a goddamn aquarium?!" She got her fingers under the first buckle, wrenching it apart with a practiced efficiency. The leather resisted — swollen, stiff, the hardware fused with water and pressure — and she worked it loose by force of will, peeling the first layer back and shoving it into the current without ceremony. It went immediately, swallowed by the dark water like it was glad to be rid of the job. The next layer followed. Then the one beneath that, canvas and lining and the waterlogged padding that had been adding weight to weight for the better part of an hour. The robe peeled over his head in sodden layers, straps slapping wetly against her arm as she tossed them aside. "You’re not dying on me because you’re too stupid to change clothes," she growled, medic’s patience long gone. Danny wheezed, eyes half-shut, but didn’t argue. No jokes. No bravado. Just silence, shivering with spent adrenaline under their hands as nearly 30 pounds of cloth came free and hit the water with a heavy slap, slowly vanishing into the darkness below. The last of the sodden layers vanished into the current behind them. Gone. Beneath all the armor and theatre, there was just... a guy. Drenched. Pale. Shaking. Human That was the thing that struck Dwight, standing there in the churning dark with his hand still on Danny's arm — the sheer unremarkability of what was underneath. Jeans. A t-shirt, soaked through and clinging. Dark hair plastered flat. A face that, without the mask and the cowl and the whole assembled architecture of the thing, was just a face. Younger than expected, maybe. Harder to read without the framing. He was still shaking. Trying not to show it, or maybe past the point of being able to manage that particular performance. Either way, he vibrated lightly in place. Jake appeared at Dwight's shoulder, angling his voice close to be heard. "We should get back to the foyer. Hall's turning everything into a whirlpool — more room to move back there. Less chance of someone else going for a swim." Dwight nodded. Looked at Danny, who was looking at nothing in particular, water dripping from his chin in a thin steady stream. "Come on," Dwight said. Not a question. Danny came. There wasn't anywhere else to go, and they all understood that without it needing to be said. The boys each took a side and helped the soaked killer navigate back along the thin beam of light, Orela’s hand at his back, as they quietly folded him into the group. Just another fish in the Entity’s fucked-up waterpark. Back in the foyer the water moved differently — the slightly wider space diffused the worst of the pressure waves into something that only shoved rather than spun. Jake peeled off toward the door without being asked, grabbed a chunk of metal debris, and started jamming it between the warped edge of the door and its swollen frame. David grunted in frustrated rhythm at his side, muscles straining as he tried again to wrench the damn thing loose. Nothing gave. The door might as well have been part of the wall itself now. Orela commandeered the flashlight from Leon with a look and turned it on Danny, running a quick efficient assessment — the cut above his hairline, the bruising already darkening along his jaw and shoulder, the way he was holding his ribs on the left side with careful stillness. His pupils tracked sluggishly, breath tight and wet. He barely seemed aware, as if he had retreated into himself and away from the chaos around them. She could barely blame him.
